title: Assistance Awards, Household Size and the Catch-Up Credit Share
content:
Financial-assistance coordination standard: the share of counted payments the catch-up credit takes on a **Patient Payment Plans** plan, according to the patient's award under the Patient Financial Assistance Program and the household size on the assistance case.

## The rule

The share of the counted payments that the catch-up credit takes depends on the patient's financial-assistance award and household:

- for a patient with an approved financial-assistance award and a household of 3 or more on the assistance case, the whole of them (100 percent);
- for a patient with an approved award and a household of fewer than 3, three quarters of them (75 percent);
- for any other patient, one half of them (50 percent).

An *approved financial-assistance award* is a case of the patient under the Patient Financial Assistance Program whose status is approved. The household is the household size recorded on that approved case. A patient whose case is still under review, or was denied, has no approved award.

## Share by award and household

| Approved award on file | Household size on the approved case | Share of the counted payments |
|---|---|---|
| Yes | 3 or more | The whole (100 percent) |
| Yes | 1 or 2 | Three quarters (75 percent) |
| No | — | One half (50 percent) |

## Boundary cases (hypothetical patients; counted payments of 60.00)

- Approved award, household of 3: the share is the whole, 60.00.
- Approved award, household of 2: the share is three quarters, 45.00.
- Application under review, household of 5: no approved award, so the share is one half, 30.00.
- No assistance case at all: one half, 30.00.

The share is taken of the counted payments and rounded to the nearest cent, an exact half cent being rounded up.
